correctness.rationale: Commutativity makes each eigenspace of one factor reducing for the rest; iteration gives a joint orthonormal eigenbasis. Successive least-tail extraction in the finitely many well-ordered coordinate sets rules out a strictly decreasing sequence of joint image values. These values are the point spectrum, not necessarily its closure. In the generic Halmos block, A_t²−A_t=−t(1−t)((I−B)⊕(I−B)), so a pure-point A_t forces B to be pure-point. Infinite distinct eigenvalues of B contain a strictly monotone subsequence; one of the strictly opposed eigenvalue branches of A_t then decreases. This proves necessity without identifying continuous spectral values with eigenvalues. Finite σ(B) makes all generic entries functions of finitely many spectral projections and gives finite σ(A_t) and a finite-dimensional generated C*-algebra; the latter in turn implies finite σ(PQP). Nongeneric blocks contribute only finitely many scalars, and an empty generic block is harmless. For the rotated direct-sum projections each positive mixture block is invertible with determinant t(1−t)sin²θ_n and trace 1, making the sum injective with zero unattained lower bound. Paired singular values sin θ_n sum geometrically to every positive power; the trace and commutator bounds follow as stated. The frozen reader checks were analytic; the supplied finite checker was inspected, not executed.
